title: Clinic support must respect operational windows
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: Seven staff supporting clinic office IT, printers, networks and backups; clinical devices excluded.
owner_narrative: Reception problems are urgent when patients are waiting, but we cannot restart systems whenever we like. Vendors handle clinical software and devices. An intermittent problem disappeared during a short visit and returned next morning. We need useful notes without patient details.

diagnostic_interview.question: Which service is in our scope?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Reception PCs and network, not clinical equipment.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: A vendor outage or clinical-device failure needs routing to the responsible supplier, not an invented IT repair procedure.

diagnostic_interview.question: Who authorizes interruption?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: The practice manager coordinates acceptable downtime.
diagnostic_interview.diagnostic_value: Work timing is an approval constraint.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: What evidence reproduces the fault?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Time, workstation and error code help; patient screenshots are unnecessary.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

diagnostic_interview.question: Was disappearance treated as resolution?
diagnostic_interview.synthetic_answer: Yes, although no cause was found.
diagnostic_interview.branch_if_answer_differs: Revise the causal hypothesis and request the corresponding source record; do not reuse this fictional answer for a new customer.

evidence.description: A simulated support agreement excludes clinical equipment.
A simulated visit has no reproduction or confirmed fix.
A simulated manager note restricts restart timing.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Scope, interruption authority and intermittent-fault evidence are missing from triage and closure criteria.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: A vendor outage or clinical-device failure needs routing to the responsible supplier, not an invented IT repair procedure.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Record operational impact using non-patient information; identify the authorized coordinator and approved work window; retain monitoring follow-up.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Guide privacy-minimizing intake, scope routing and authorization tracking; draft updates without clinical details.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: Do not collect patient records for routine IT triage.
requirements.rationale: Scope, interruption authority and intermittent-fault evidence are missing from triage and closure criteria.

requirements.statement: Disruptive changes require current scope-specific approval.
requirements.rationale: Scope, interruption authority and intermittent-fault evidence are missing from triage and closure criteria.

requirements.statement: Not reproduced remains distinct from confirmed resolution.
requirements.rationale: Scope, interruption authority and intermittent-fault evidence are missing from triage and closure criteria.

requirements.statement: Clinical advice and clinical-device procedures stay outside this case.
requirements.rationale: Scope, interruption authority and intermittent-fault evidence are missing from triage and closure criteria.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: A patient-bearing screenshot is flagged for controlled handling, not indexed.
No restart is scheduled outside the approved window.
A recurring symptom reopens investigation with prior evidence.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Operational-window and privacy controls require explicit engineering and customer review.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Unplanned service interruption minutes caused by maintenance; track recurrence and time to appropriate supplier engagement.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Record operational impact using non-patient information; identify the authorized coordinator and approved work window; retain monitoring follow-up. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: A vendor outage or clinical-device failure needs routing to the responsible supplier, not an invented IT repair procedure.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Customer privacy procedures, criticality and exact authorization policy need local confirmation.

transfer_rules.do_not_assume: A vendor outage or clinical-device failure needs routing to the responsible supplier, not an invented IT repair procedure.
